summary: Specifies a shared LISP message type for defining future extensions and running experiments without using up a LISP Packet Type codepoint for each one. It also creates an IANA registry for these extensions. It obsoletes RFC 8113. It is a standards-track specification.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 9304 reserves LISP packet type 15 as a shared message for extensions and experiments. Each extension uses a registered subtype, so it does not need its own packet-type codepoint; RFC 9304 obsoletes RFC 8113.

subtitle: A shared LISP message type for future extensions and experiments

tldr.problem: LISP has a limited packet-type space, while extensions and experiments need identifiers.
tldr.mechanism: The shared extension message uses packet type 15 and a registered subtype to identify each extension; its extension-specific structure is defined separately.
tldr.outcome: RFC 9304 creates a subtype registry and obsoletes RFC 8113.

facts.label: First Come, First Served subtype range

today: RFC 9304 obsoletes RFC 8113 and is a Standards Track specification.

sections.title: A Shared Type for LISP Extensions
sections.content:
The LISP base specification identifies packet types with codepoints, and the available type space is limited. The RFC expects additional LISP extensions and describes a need to experiment with them without allocating a separate packet type for each one.

It defines one shared extension message type. A subtype uniquely identifies the particular extension that uses the shared message.
sections.plainLanguage: Instead of assigning each extension a separate packet type, LISP can use one shared type and distinguish extensions with subtypes.

sections.title: The Shared Message Format
sections.content: The message begins with a type field set to 15, followed by a subtype field. The subtype MUST be registered with IANA. The rest of the message is extension-specific, and the specification for that extension defines its structure.
sections.plainLanguage: The shared message uses type 15 and a registered subtype. The subtype tells the reader which extension defines the rest of the message.

sections.title: Subtype Registration and Status
sections.content:
IANA maintains a LISP Shared Extension Message Type Sub-types registry. Values from 0 through 1023 are assigned via Standards Action. Values from 1024 through 4095 are assigned First Come, First Served; a request gives IANA the desired codepoint and a point of contact, and a short description is encouraged.

This RFC changes the status from Experimental to Standards Track and obsoletes RFC 8113.
sections.plainLanguage: Some subtype numbers require Standards Action, while a higher range uses First Come, First Served. RFC 9304 is Standards Track and replaces RFC 8113.
